extracted.intended_audience: corporate communications teams, PR professionals, and crisis-management advisers
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of lessons and evaluative criteria drawn from historical PR disasters, aimed at guiding corporate communications and crisis management decisions to avoid reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show empathy and compassion
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate apparent empathy and compassion in public statements and responses to crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BP Oil crisis highlights how a lack of apparent empathy (e.g., comments like “I’d like my life back”) evokes public resentment and escalates backlash. Guidance: prioritize human-focused messaging, acknowledge harm, avoid dismissive or self-centered language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear, comprehensive information and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Make detailed information about the incident readily available through official channels and keep stakeholders updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BP’s website had scant information and minimal social links; this exacerbated the crisis. Guidance: maintain an up-to-date, information-rich hub (website/social feeds) with FAQs, steps being taken, and contact points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond quickly and issue immediate statements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a damaging incident surfaces, issue an appropriate, timely public response rather than waiting or hoping it fades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domino’s were criticised for not issuing an immediate statement after damaging employee videos spread. Guidance: prepare holding statements, acknowledge the situation, and outline immediate actions while investigations continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t delete or silence criticism; engage constructively
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid deleting critical comments or silencing critics; instead, acknowledge concerns and engage transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nestlé deleted many Facebook comments during Greenpeace action, which provoked further criticism. Guidance: use engagement, clarifying information, and meaningful responses rather than deletion, unless comments violate clear policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be culturally sensitive and avoid offensive creative content
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure advertising and creative content do not exploit trauma, marginalised groups, or sensitive subjects for messages that can be perceived as offensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ogilvy’s ad using Malala Yousafzai imagery (showing her shot) caused outrage. Urban Outfitters’ sale of a racist board game provoked heavy criticism. Guidance: vet creative for cultural sensitivity, consider external review, and reject edgy content that trades on real suffering or stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sincere apologies and corrective actions when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue clear apologies and outline concrete remedial steps when at fault, rather than vague or perfunctory statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ogilvy apologised directly to Malala’s family; Netflix’s CEO publicly apologised for the Qwikster decision. Guidance: apologies should be personal, acknowledge responsibility, and be paired with specific corrective actions and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and prepare for social media virality and meme responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that stories can spawn jokes, memes and rapid sharing; monitor channels closely and plan responses accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The horsemeat scandal spawned memes and infographics that shaped public perception. Guidance: have social listening in place, anticipate viral frames, and respond fast to correct misinformation or calm outrage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reactive, aggressive social-media engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not respond to criticism with defensive or combative messaging that damages tone and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tinder’s 30-tweet tirade against Vanity Fair was seen as losing the cool in front of the audience. Guidance: social teams should follow escalation protocols and tone guidelines; never 'lose your cool' publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control employee behaviour and enforce operational safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure staff conduct, hygiene and access controls prevent internally generated brand harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Domino’s YouTube scandal involved employees performing disgusting acts on food. Guidance: enforce clear employee codes of conduct, surveillance/controls where appropriate, and rapid disciplinary processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate regulatory and broadcast sensitivities for live events
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for live-broadcast risks and regulatory exposure; implement safeguards and delay mechanisms as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Janet Jackson’s Super Bowl incident led to hundreds of thousands of complaints and new broadcasting rules. Guidance: use broadcast delays, clear content protocols, and compliance checks for live programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate major business changes transparently to customers
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing pricing, services or packages, communicate clearly, honestly and with customer-focused rationale to avoid perceptions of bad faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Netflix’s unbundling/Qwikster announcements and reversals caused customer anger and share-price damage. Guidance: test messaging, explain benefits, and avoid sudden moves that will be perceived as a price hike or downgrade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize legal/technical correctness does not equal public acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Even legal behaviour (e.g., tax minimisation) can cause severe reputational damage if perceived as unethical by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax avoidance stories about Amazon, Google and Starbucks were legal but harmed public opinion and led to social media campaigns. Guidance: consider reputational impacts of legal strategies and adopt transparency or ethical stances where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about sourcing and supply-chain practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose and improve sourcing practices to avoid credibility attacks related to environmental or ethical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greenpeace’s palm-oil campaign pressured Nestlé into stopping unsustainable sourcing. Guidance: proactively audit supply chains, communicate commitments, and be ready with evidence of responsible sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate third-party activism and the benefits of conceding when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize activist campaigns can gain momentum quickly; engaging constructively or changing practices may be the most effective resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nestlé’s eventual decision to stop sourcing unsustainable palm oil was a win for Greenpeace. Guidance: evaluate activist claims, engage in dialogue, and be prepared to change practices rather than only defending reputation.
